analysis:
Examined both configuration excerpts, protocol file metadata and all supplied protocol hunks against the canonical index and detailed T-041. No concrete security regression is established by these documentation-only units. Configuration lines 478–734 are unchanged per the complete range map: cache opt-ins, scope, TTL, encryption, debug-key restrictions, memory admission and attestation controls described there cannot be attributed to this PR. The configuration change at head 180–186 is only partially supplied, limiting review of scheduled-window inventory retention.
Protocol changes introduce consent-gated inventory downloads, dynamic adoption of verified catalog builds under unchanged consent revision (head 1380, 1470–1486), storage/busy telemetry (1391–1419), and placement holds plus serving after lease expiry (1230, 1514–1516). Documented catalog/hash checks, operator download controls, capacity bounds and separation from ordinary models_update provide relevant safeguards; there is no demonstrated consumer-controlled authorization or plaintext exposure. The coordinator remains trusted and provider observations must not become authoritative capacity or serving evidence.
Integration must inspect AutopilotDownload.swift, AutopilotModelSet, CoordinatorClientCodec.swift and lifecycle/load admission code: verify consent revocation before publication, inventory/hash snapshot consistency, private_only isolation, download-cap accounting and concurrent work, and bounded hold cleanup. In particular, verify adopted serving after an Autopilot lease ends still requires current connection-bound serving authorization (A-016, T-052/T-053, TB-011), and holds cannot bypass memory admission or update/drain cancellation (TB-007, T-029). These are unverified implementation contracts, not observed missing controls. T-041's RAM-tier assumptions differ from unchanged configuration documentation and are not shown to be newly invalidated here. Remaining uncertainty requires implementation integration review.
